title: Prefere a structural splice over regenerating the whole module
summary: When you change one Python method, do not regenerate the file from a partial model in your head: rewrite only the exact source span of that method and leave every unrelated import, comment, sibling method, docstring and byte-formatted newline untouched. Whole-module regeneration from memory is the most destructive LLM habit and the direct cause of collateral damage.
semantics: The engine editors (source.python.method.edit / source.oorexx.method.edit) implement exactly this invariant: an edit changes only the declared target region unless wider transformation was explicitly requested. Replacement fragments are one complete method; the module is re-parsed before commit.
why_this_is_an_article: It is a working-method discipline on how to perform the edit, not a single deterministic language trigger.
evidence_note: PLABEL: ties to LLM Gopher's own source-edit invariant (engine/README v0.6). It is universal good practice when editing any codebase.
invariants: Edit confined to the target method's source span (AST-derived class/method node), not a manual byte guess.
Preserve unrelated comments, imports, sibling methods and formatting byte-for-byte.
Replace only with one complete, parseable method; validate the whole module before committing.
Carry an expected_sha256 when present so a moved/stale source is rejected instead of silently mis-spliced.
Match the module's prevailing newline convention when you reindent a supplied fragment.
